questions: Déf. 3 requires V Hausdorff (read « variété », plan F6): without it « Cette définition est indépendante de la carte f choisie » fails — on ]0,∞[ with the point 1 doubled (n = 1, GU(1) = {±1}), the identity charts of the two copies are cone charts with transition id and ½·2 is 1 in one chart, 1' in the other (described, not formalized). Is Hausdorff to be read into « variété » here, as in plan F6?

Does V Hausdorff (with Déf. 2's 3°) force the base B = V/ℝ⁺ to be Hausdorff? Not proved here; sufficient: the ℝ₊* action is proper (t2Space_of_properSMul). It matters for Déf. 3's « topologiquement trivial » (a section forces B Hausdorff: t2Space_of_section) and for wave 4's equivalence (F(B) is Hausdorff only over Hausdorff B). A naive counterexample (W = {x>0} ⊂ ℝ²−0 modulo diag(2,½)) violates 3°, which is what excludes it.
